title: Enterprise Deployment: Azure Container Apps, Bicep IaC & GitHub Actions CI/CD
description: Deploy EnterpriseNexus to production Azure: Infrastructure as Code (Bicep), Azure Container Apps with KEDA autoscaling, Managed Identity zero-secret authentication, GitHub Actions OIDC pipelines, and Application Insights observability.

data.text: Production Cloud Architecture for Enterprise AI

Deploying an enterprise AI assistant requires modern cloud infrastructure tailored for bursty AI workloads. Azure Container Apps (ACA) provides serverless microcontainer hosting built on Kubernetes (AKS) and KEDA, offering built-in HTTPS ingress, automatic TLS, and dynamic scale-to-zero capabilities. Crucially, production security demands a zero-secret architecture where connection strings and API keys are completely eradicated in favor of Microsoft Entra Managed Identities and Azure RBAC.

data.text: We define the entire infrastructure declaratively using Azure Bicep. Notice how the container app is assigned a User-Assigned Managed Identity, and RBAC role assignments grant direct access to Azure OpenAI without storing an API key anywhere in configuration.

data.content: Deploying the .NET 9 API container with Managed Identity and Cognitive Services OpenAI User role assignment.

data.text: Enterprise container images must be minimal, contain zero shell utilities (like bash or curl), and run under an unprivileged non-root user. Microsoft's 'chiseled' Ubuntu images reduce attack surfaces and vulnerability scanning alerts to zero.

data.title: Dockerfile for EnterpriseNexus.WebApi
data.content: Production multi-stage build targeting .NET 9 with chiseled non-root base.
data.code:
# 1. Build Stage
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Copy csproj and restore layers
COPY ["EnterpriseNexus.WebApi/EnterpriseNexus.WebApi.csproj", "EnterpriseNexus.WebApi/"]
COPY ["EnterpriseNexus.Application/EnterpriseNexus.Application.csproj", "EnterpriseNexus.Application/"]
COPY ["EnterpriseNexus.Domain/EnterpriseNexus.Domain.csproj", "EnterpriseNexus.Domain/"]
COPY ["EnterpriseNexus.Infrastructure/EnterpriseNexus.Infrastructure.csproj", "EnterpriseNexus.Infrastructure/"]
RUN dotnet restore "EnterpriseNexus.WebApi/EnterpriseNexus.WebApi.csproj"

# Copy source and publish
COPY . .
WORKDIR "/src/EnterpriseNexus.WebApi"
RUN dotnet publish "EnterpriseNexus.WebApi.csproj" -c Release -o /app/publish /p:UseAppHost=false

# 2. Runtime Stage (Chiseled, non-root, ultra-secure)
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:9.0-noble-chiseled AS final
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/publish .
USER $APP_UID
EXPOSE 8080
ENV ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS=8080
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "EnterpriseNexus.WebApi.dll"]

data.text: The CI/CD pipeline deploys to Azure without storing static subscription secrets or passwords in GitHub, using OpenID Connect (OIDC) federated credentials.

data.title: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
data.content: Automated build, test, container push, and Bicep deployment via GitHub Actions OIDC.
data.code:
name: EnterpriseNexus Production Deployment

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  id-token: write # Required for Azure OIDC
  contents: read

jobs:
  test-and-deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup .NET 9
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with:
          dotnet-version: '9.0.x'

      - name: Run Test Suite & AI Evaluations
        run: |
          dotnet test --configuration Release --logger "trx;LogFileName=test_results.trx"

      - name: Azure Login via OIDC
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      - name: Build & Push Container to Azure Container Registry
        run: |
          az acr build --registry acrnexusprod --image nexus-api:${{ github.sha }} -f EnterpriseNexus.WebApi/Dockerfile .

      - name: Deploy Bicep Infrastructure & Container App
        uses: azure/arm-deploy@v2
        with:
          scope: resourcegroup
          resourceGroupName: rg-enterprise-nexus-prod
          template: ./infra/main.bicep
          parameters: >
            apiImageName=acrnexusprod.azurecr.io/nexus-api:${{ github.sha }}

data.title: Production Deployment Go-Live Checklist
items: Zero hardcoded connection strings or API keys; Entra ID Managed Identity used exclusively
Container images built on chiseled distroless bases running as non-root user ($APP_UID)
GitHub Actions authenticates via OIDC federated credentials, eliminating long-lived secrets
Azure Container Apps scaling rules configured: HTTP concurrency for WebApi, queue depth for Ingestion
Private endpoints and VNet integration configured for PostgreSQL, Azure OpenAI, and Blob Storage
Health probes (/healthz/live, /healthz/ready) active and reporting to ACA orchestrator
Application Insights distributed tracing active with custom metrics for AI latency and token cost

data.title: Summary & Capstone Conclusion
points: Azure Container Apps provides the optimal serverless hosting environment for enterprise AI microservices.
Bicep IaC with Managed Identity establishes a zero-secret security baseline across all Azure resources.
Chiseled Ubuntu containers eliminate common CVE vulnerabilities and attack surfaces.
With Phase 7 complete, you have designed, built, and deployed an enterprise-grade AI Knowledge Assistant.
data.takeaway: Enterprise AI readiness is defined by cloud maturity: declarative infrastructure, secretless authentication, automated CI/CD, and elastic autoscaling.
